title: Adobe Acrobat Pricing: 2026 Plans, Costs, and Options
summary: Adobe Acrobat pricing varies by plan and billing method. Review the costs of each option to see what you'll actually pay.
body_markdown:
## Automate PDF handoffs around Acrobat with Activepieces


If manual handoffs are what's costing you, Activepieces earns a place: it's a workflow tool with 746 integrations in an MIT-licensed core, enough to take over the copying, filing and nagging that happens around your PDFs. It doesn't edit or sign anything.


If your real pain is that nobody can find the signed contract or the approver never saw the request, this is the cheaper fix. If your pain is editing text inside a PDF, skip it and keep the Acrobat plan that covers that.


Doing nothing here has a price too.


Someone on your team is saving a signed file, renaming it, dragging it into a shared folder and messaging a colleague. Every one of those steps is a chance for the file to land in the wrong place or sit unseen.


On an Adobe invoice that time never shows up, but you pay it in wages.


Activepieces doesn't multiply that cost by seat the way Acrobat does: its Free plan is $0 for up to 5 users, with unlimited flows and 1,000 credits a month, a run costs 1 credit however many steps it has, and Alan and Funding Societies run it in production, proving that the free plan works in real production environments, so you defer licensing costs until your team grows beyond five people.


Picture the canvas in the screenshot below, where each step is a box in a vertical line: a new lead arrives from HubSpot, an AI step qualifies it, and a yes-or-no check sends it down one path.


The later steps add it to Salesforce, post to Slack and send an email through Gmail.


It is a sales example, but the shape is what matters. You pick a trigger, then stack the actions that follow it, with no code involved.


Swap the trigger for "signed PDF lands in a folder" and the same shape files the document, tells the approver and moves the file along.


For sign-off chains, the tool's "Human Approval" tab suggests a step that waits for a person to say yes before the flow continues. Start with one handoff, the one your team complains about most, and build only that.
